new_candidates.body:
**Describe the bug**

With a subscription history depth above 1, `rcl_take` can return samples of one topic out of order: N+1 before N. This happens when several samples are buffered within one clock tick.

[`rmw_uxrce_find_static_input_buffer_by_owner`](https://github.com/micro-ROS/rmw_microxrcedds/blob/cbc4a1e60aeafd051a7c1636045653d5df425f98/rmw_microxrcedds_c/src/types.c#L286) picks the oldest buffer by timestamp with a strict comparison:

```c
if (data->owner == owner && data->timestamp < min_time) {
```

Three things combine:

1. A reliable stream that receives a missing sample late delivers the held samples right after it. On my board they arrive about 50 µs apart, so several can get the same timestamp.
2. `get_memory` inserts new items at the head of the list, so the walk sees the newest buffer first.
3. With a strict `<`, a tie keeps the first buffer seen, which is the newest one.

**To Reproduce**

1. Use a reliable subscription with `RMW_UXRCE_MAX_HISTORY` above 1, and publish a sequence counter on its topic.
2. Run on a link that reorders or delays datagrams, so the reliable stream has to hold samples back. I use an access point that adds 0-200 ms of random delay in each direction.
3. Check that each taken value is one above the previous one. Occasionally two neighbouring values come back swapped.

I do not have a hardware-free reproduction for this one. The list order and the comparison can be checked by reading `get_memory` and the function above.

**Expected behaviour**

Samples of one subscription are taken in arrival order, including when timestamps tie.

**System information**

- OS: Zephyr 4.1.0 on ESP32-C6, UDP over Wi-Fi
- ROS 2: Jazzy
- Version: `e64d79f`. The comparison is unchanged on `jazzy` (`cbc4a1e`) and `kilted` (`9d49b4d`).

**Additional context**

Results on the board:

| Change | Result |
|---|---|
| Strictly increasing timestamps | No swaps |
| `<` changed to `<=` | No swaps, with 22 ties seen during the run |
| 10 kHz system tick | Fewer swaps, but they still occur |

Swaps only happen within one topic. They also occur with the Client multithread profile off.

**Proposed fix**

I would give each buffer an arrival counter and compare that instead:

```c
if (data->owner == owner && (ret == NULL || (int32_t)(data->arrival_seq - min_seq) < 0)) {
```

`<=` also passes the test above, but it relies on the list being in newest-first order. A counter states the arrival order directly, and the signed difference handles wraparound. `timestamp` stays because the lifespan check needs it. I have not validated this form on the board yet, and can open a PR once I have.
new_candidates.title: Samples can be taken out of order when static input buffers have equal timestamps
